claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a son named Alex who is 8 years old and lives with you at home.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? By this I mean, do you provide for his daily needs such as food, clothes, and pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's been in local authority care for a few months now, so the council is looking after his daily needs during that time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**How many weeks has Alex been in local authority care? Has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been about 12 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions to help determine your eligibility:

**During these 12 weeks that Alex has been in care, does he spend any regular time at home with you? For example, does he come home for at least 24 hours per week, or spend at least 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home regularly like that. He's been at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the council is paying for his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks, which is more than the 8-week limit set by the Child Benefit rules. When a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks, parents usually lose their entitlement to Child Benefit.

There are exceptions to this rule - for example, if Alex was spending at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or at least 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 or more days in a row at home. However, since Alex has been at the care home full-time and doesn't come home regularly, and the council is paying for his accommodation and maintenance, these exceptions don't apply in your situation.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he starts spending regular time at home with you - you may want to contact HMRC to see if you could claim Child Benefit again at that point.
